thread.title: Asia Markets: Asian markets roll along on Powell’s comments; Nikkei up for 5th straight day

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Asia Markets: Asian markets roll along on Powell’s comments; Nikkei up for 5th straight day
text:
Asian stock markets logged solid gains in early trading Thursday after the 2%-plus jumps in the U.S. as Fed Chairman Jerome Powell’s comments Wednesday hinted at a slower pace of Fed rate increases next year.
Japanese stocks were up for the fifth straight session on gains led by the energy sector after the price of crude fell to 13-month lows. The Nikkei
 NIK, +0.39%
 was 0.9% higher. Among individual stocks , Nintendo
 7974, +4.06%
 was up more than 4% and SoftBank
 9984, +3.06%
 gained more than 3%. Still, some risk persists. With the dollar
 JPYUSD, +0.292006%
 sitting around ¥113.42 compared with ¥113.68 in late New York trade, the 20-year JGB’s yield was lower by half a basis point at 0.605%.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index
 HSI, -0.87%
 gave up early gains and was last down 0.2%. Index heavyweight Tencent
 0700, -0.89%
 fell more than 1% while property developer Sun Hung Kai Properties
 2949, -1.47%
 advanced 1%.
China’s benchmarks were slightly higher, with investors are on their toes for the weekend meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. The Shanghai Composite
 SHCOMP, -1.32%
 and the Shenzhen Composite
 399106, -2.21%
 swung between slight gains and losses and were last up fractionally. But Nomura analysts remain wary of the trade summit, calling the meeting “a high stakes dinner but the menu might not include a trade deal.”
South Korea’s Kospi
 SEU, +0.28%
 rose 0.5% as Samsung
 005930, +0.00%
 gained slightly. Taiwan’s Taiex
 Y9999, +0.01%
 gained 0.5% as Apple Inc.
 AAPL, +3.85%
 suppliers Largan Precision
 3008, +1.15%
 and Taiwan Semiconductor
 2330, +1.10%
 advanced . Singapore’s benchmark index
 STI, +0.56%
 was up nearly 1%.
Down Under, Australia’s ASX 200
 XJO, +0.58%
 improved 0.4%, with Rio Tinto
 RIO, +1.74%
 and BHP Billiton
 BHP, +1.21%
 each up more than 1%. New Zealand’s benchmark
 NZ50GR, +0.93%
 rose about 1%.
